questions.stem: Which of these is NOT included in the definition of survival craft in the Fire and Boat Drills Regulations?
options: A lifejacket
A life raft
A lifeboat
An inflatable rescue platform
questions.explanation: Survival craft means a lifeboat, rescue boat, emergency boat, suitable boat, buoyant apparatus, life raft, inflatable rescue platform or any other vessel capable of sustaining lives from the time of abandoning the vessel. A lifejacket is a personal life-saving appliance, not a craft.

questions.stem: What is a rescue boat designed to do?
options: Rescue persons in distress and marshal survival craft
Carry the ship's cargo ashore
Replace the ship's lifeboats permanently
Tow the ship in an emergency
questions.explanation: The regulations define a rescue boat as a boat designed to be used for rescuing persons in distress and marshalling survival craft. It is not a cargo boat or a towing vessel.

questions.stem: Which marine emergency duties training does a Bridge Watch Rating candidate need in addition to basic safety?
options: Proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats other than fast rescue boats
Proficiency in fast rescue boats only
Offshore firefighting
Small seasonal passenger vessel safety only
questions.explanation: The Marine Personnel Regulations s. 171 table for the Bridge Watch Rating lists MED training in proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats other than fast rescue boats. Fast rescue boats are a separate course, not required here.

questions.stem: Under MPR s. 205(6), who must hold a training certificate in proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats other than fast rescue boats?
options: Every person assigned on the muster list to preparing or launching a survival craft, other than a manually launched life raft or manually launched inflatable rescue platform
Only the master
Every passenger
Only the cook
questions.explanation: Section 205(6) puts the certificate requirement on those assigned on the muster list to prepare or launch survival craft, except for manually launched life rafts and inflatable rescue platforms. Passengers and non-assigned crew are not covered by that subsection.

questions.stem: Before a survival craft drill, who must have a list of the survival craft crew members?
options: The person in charge of the survival craft and the second-in-command
Only the master
Only the passengers' representative
No one; lists are not used
questions.explanation: Section 25(1) says the person in charge of a survival craft and his or her second-in-command each have a list of the crew members, and the person in charge makes sure the crew know their duties.

questions.stem: A vessel has two lifeboats. How must lifeboats be launched in survival craft drills under the Fire and Boat Drills Regulations?
options: A different lifeboat is launched in each drill, and each lifeboat is launched and manoeuvred in the water by the assigned crew at least once every three months
The same lifeboat is launched each time and the other is never launched
Each lifeboat is launched every week
Lifeboats are launched only after an actual emergency
questions.explanation: Section 27(1) requires a different lifeboat in each survival craft drill and each lifeboat to be launched and manoeuvred in the water at least once every three months. At sea the launching may be replaced by clearing and swinging out, if each is still launched every three months.

questions.stem: A vessel carries a rescue boat that is not a lifeboat. How often must a rescue boat drill be held, and how?
options: At least once a month, separately from any other drill, with the crew launching and manoeuvring the rescue boat in the water
Once a year, as part of the fire drill
Every three months, without launching
Only when passengers are on board
questions.explanation: Section 31 requires a rescue boat drill at least once a month, held separately from any other drill, in which the crew launch and manoeuvre the boat in the water. Lifeboats, including those that are rescue boats, follow the three-monthly rule in s. 27.

questions.stem: The vessel is under way and a lifeboat launching drill is due. How must it be carried out, and what else must the crew be able to do under s. 26?
options: In sheltered waters under the supervision of an experienced officer; and crew must be able to don the immersion suits or anti-exposure suits carried
In open water at full speed with no supervision; and crew need not handle immersion suits
Only alongside, never under way; and crew must be able to swim 100 m
In any water so long as passengers are ashore
questions.explanation: Sections 27(3) and 31(3) require launching and manoeuvring drills under way to be carried out in sheltered waters under an officer experienced in launchings and manoeuvrings while under way, and s. 26 requires crew to be capable of donning the immersion suits or marine anti-exposure suits carried on the vessel.

questions.stem: A 9 m passenger-carrying vessel (SVR Part 4) works in the open Strait of Georgia, not on a sheltered waters voyage and more than two nautical miles from any river or lake shore. What does SVR s. 411 require?
options: Life rafts with a total capacity sufficient for all persons on board
No life raft, because the vessel is under 12 m
Only lifejackets
A rescue boat with an engine
questions.explanation: Section 411(2) requires life rafts for everyone on board unless the vessel is not more than 8.5 m in length, on a sheltered waters voyage, or within two nautical miles of the shore of a river or lake. A 9 m vessel in the open strait meets none of those exceptions, so she needs the rafts.

questions.stem: A small passenger-carrying vessel under SVR Part 4 carries no life raft and the water is 10 degrees Celsius. What must the operator do?
options: Make sure equipment is carried or procedures are established to protect all persons from hypothermia or cold shock
Nothing, because the rule applies only below 5 degrees Celsius
Cancel the voyage
Provide hot drinks only
questions.explanation: Section 403 applies when the water temperature is less than 15 degrees Celsius and no life raft is carried: equipment must be carried or procedures established to protect everyone from hypothermia or cold shock resulting from swamping, capsizing or falling overboard. The temperature trigger is 15, not 5, and the rule does not require cancelling the voyage.
